text:
• Mandatory waypoints
• Restricted area

• Length of the route in km
• Duration of the trip in min (in accordance with the speed limits and not exceeding 80 km/h)
• Continuity of the route relying on the road network
• The routes must be within the deployment area
• The routes cannot go through the restricted area
• Two strictly different routes from PD5 to PA5 then from PA5 to PD5
• Both routes must be as fast as possible from PD5 to PA5 and from PA5 to PD5
• The duration of the trip must be calculated taking into account the legal speed limits on each part of the route.
• The route must be as short as possible from PD5 to PA5 going through all the waypoints in the order WP1, WP2, WP3, WP4 on the way in; you will not go through the waypoints on the way back. For this exercise, we need you to find two routes connecting the Point of Departure to the Point of Arrival (outbound and return, which must be strictly different). You need to go through all the waypoints in the order WP1, WP2, WP3, WP4 on the way in. You won’t cross the waypoints on your way back. You can only use the network within the Deployment Area. You can’t use any of the roads within the Restricted Area. You must find the shortest route. You will have to return a layout representing the route and indicate the length in kilometres as well as the estimated duration of the trip.

Deconfliction is the spatial and temporal coordination of military movements to prevent conflicts between convoys sharing the same routes or junction.
